hints.title: Adjacent Duplicate Bypass Obstacle
hints.text: Retaining adjacent duplicates leaves identical values in the sorted sequence. How can you skip a node whenever its value matches the preceding element?

hints.title: Single-Link Skipping Invariant
hints.text: Iterate curr through the list and if curr.val equals curr.next.val, point curr.next to curr.next.next without advancing curr.

hints.title: In-Place Value Comparison Procedure
hints.text: Initialize curr at head. While curr and curr.next are not null, compare their values. If equal, update curr.next to curr.next.next. Otherwise, advance curr to curr.next. Return head.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 300)
complexity.notes: Single linear pass bypassing duplicate links in-place.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Building a new list uses extra memory, whereas in-place skipping requires zero auxiliary allocations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Comparing adjacent node values in sorted order requires O(1) space without secondary sets.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Ensuring curr is only advanced when curr.val != curr.next.val (to handle 3+ duplicate nodes).
